scope: Original conditional rules for PRISM Studio rebuild and future product workflows; not installed application behaviour.

rules.principle: Design around the user's task and constraints.
rules.appliesWhen: Starting or reassessing a screen, flow or run.
rules.action: State the intended user, task, success condition and constraints before choosing layouts or infrastructure.
rules.check: The proposed flow exposes a recognizable next action and an observable success condition.
exceptions: Exploratory discovery can keep hypotheses open; label them instead of inventing certainty.

rules.principle: Keep observations, policy and proposals distinguishable.
rules.appliesWhen: Recording findings, decisions or implementation guidance.
rules.action: Label current behaviour, proposed behaviour, user decisions, source advice and measured results separately.
rules.check: A reader can identify what exists, what is intended and what evidence supports each material claim.
exceptions: An unresolved fact remains unknown; a confident writing style does not change its status.

rules.principle: Retrieve the smallest context sufficient for the task.
rules.appliesWhen: Building a worker packet or selecting references.
rules.action: Include the active skill, correct repository instructions, exact inputs, owned scope and selected rule IDs; retrieve source sections on demand.
rules.check: Packet size and sources are recorded; AGENTS and required contracts are present without whole-book injection.
exceptions: Expand context when a concrete unresolved risk requires it; do not omit necessary evidence merely to hit a token target.

rules.principle: Check the version and authority of operational advice.
rules.appliesWhen: Using prices, protocols, models, host flags or historical code.
rules.action: Resolve current primary documentation or observed capabilities and retain the source date and applicable version.
rules.check: No retired recipe or unverified model/price is presented as current capability.
exceptions: Durable conceptual reasoning may remain useful without re-reading the whole source.

rules.principle: Treat psychology and visual heuristics as conditional.
rules.appliesWhen: Using a named law, count limit or example to justify a design.
rules.action: Explain the relevant task and tradeoff; externalize required information and evaluate actual behaviour.
rules.check: No universal menu count, ROI promise or unsupported causal score is used as a gate.
exceptions: Directly applicable primary evidence can support a narrower quantitative claim with its conditions.

rules.principle: Keep frequent actions visible and disclose rare complexity.
rules.appliesWhen: Balancing novice guidance with expert repeat work.
rules.action: Group information by task, expose common actions and preserve optional expansion state; test the added effort of hidden controls.
rules.check: The primary repeat task does not require avoidable disclosure on every pass.
exceptions: A dense professional surface can be appropriate; progressive disclosure is not a universal reduction in controls.

rules.principle: Name controls and errors by their user-facing purpose.
rules.appliesWhen: Creating buttons, form fields, navigation or validation.
rules.action: Use meaningful accessible names, visible labels where needed, linked field errors and recovery instructions.
rules.check: Keyboard and accessible-tree checks identify each control and correction without relying on placeholder or colour.
exceptions: An established icon can be visually compact, but its accessible name and context remain necessary.

rules.principle: Separate visual priority from semantic structure.
rules.appliesWhen: Styling headings, labels, actions or dense information.
rules.action: Use size, weight, contrast and spacing to express priority while preserving correct headings, labels and reading order.
rules.check: The visual and semantic structures support the same task; style changes do not remove names or meaning.
exceptions: Secondary text still needs applicable contrast; semantic correctness does not mandate identical visual weight.

rules.principle: Use coherent tokens with verified state combinations.
rules.appliesWhen: Creating or changing a theme or shared component.
rules.action: Define semantic colours, typography, spacing, focus and motion states; test actual backgrounds and interactions.
rules.check: Supported themes pass applicable contrast/focus checks and preserve recognizable state meaning.
exceptions: An existing sound system can be reused; no specific spacing grid or font count is compulsory.

rules.principle: Adapt to content and input capability.
rules.appliesWhen: Designing desktop, narrow, touch or zoomed layouts.
rules.action: Keep the expert task usable while supporting reflow, reachable controls and appropriate coarse-pointer targets.
rules.check: Exercise narrow/wide, keyboard/touch and enlarged layouts; record any criterion-specific two-dimensional exception.
exceptions: A canvas or table may legitimately require two-dimensional navigation; surrounding controls still need usable reflow.

rules.principle: Preserve predictable keyboard and focus behaviour.
rules.appliesWhen: Implementing navigation, dialogs, updates or composite widgets.
rules.action: Use native patterns, visible focus, logical movement, sensible dialog focus return and no focus theft during background updates.
rules.check: Complete the primary flows with keyboard controls and verify active focus after updates and dialog exit.
exceptions: Use conventional roving-focus patterns inside composites; every internal element need not be a separate Tab stop.

rules.principle: Provide a distinct non-drag pointer path.
rules.appliesWhen: An interaction uses dragging.
rules.action: Offer click/tap endpoints, move controls or an equivalent input for the same result, in addition to keyboard support.
rules.check: Complete the operation using a single pointer without dragging; document any narrow essential exception.
exceptions: Essential freehand behaviour may need a criterion-specific exception; this does not exempt selection, movement or other controls.

sourceLocators.P02: Intent and separation from keyboard accessibility

rules.principle: Measure hit areas and spacing rather than icon size alone.
rules.appliesWhen: Building pointer controls or dense action groups.
rules.action: Meet applicable SC 2.5.8 size or exception conditions; prefer larger primary touch targets where feasible.
rules.check: Measure actual hit boxes and spacing in each supported layout.
exceptions: WCAG AA, AAA and native-platform points are distinct; do not present 44 CSS px as the universal AA minimum.

rules.principle: Keep state legible without colour alone.
rules.appliesWhen: Displaying decisions, connection, errors, budget or charts.
rules.action: Pair colour with text, symbols or structure and meet applicable text/non-text contrast.
rules.check: All supported themes and relevant states remain distinguishable in non-colour and contrast checks.
exceptions: Do not infer overall accessibility conformance from one contrast measurement.

rules.principle: Provide truthful feedback without distracting repetition.
rules.appliesWhen: Work is slow, asynchronous or repeatedly refreshed.
rules.action: Acknowledge actions, show actual known progress, preserve cancel/recovery and announce meaningful milestones with reduced-motion support.
rules.check: A stalled task is distinguishable from activity; polling does not steal focus or repeatedly flood announcements.
exceptions: Use indeterminate progress when a percentage is unknown; do not simulate effort or completion.

rules.principle: Choose image alternatives by purpose.
rules.appliesWhen: Adding an image, icon, chart or artifact preview.
rules.action: Describe meaningful information or function; use empty alt for appropriate decorative images; expose artifact metadata and useful text context.
rules.check: Alternative text matches the role and does not duplicate decorative noise.
exceptions: Complex visual work may need an adjacent description or data view beyond a short alt attribute.

rules.principle: Review real immutable artifacts and identify derivatives.
rules.appliesWhen: Presenting work for approval or comparison.
rules.action: Render the retained artifact safely, label version/source, and keep full-resolution access; distinguish preview captures from authoritative source bytes.
rules.check: A reviewer can identify and inspect the exact version being decided on; failed rendering is visible.
exceptions: Unsupported formats remain unsupported; a placeholder or successful thumbnail does not prove source rendering.

rules.principle: Bind decisions to exact relevant inputs.
rules.appliesWhen: Recording an approval, rejection or change request.
rules.action: Use the artifact/component version, dependency fingerprint and expected request revision; record actor and optional/conditional fields consistently.
rules.check: The same valid decision succeeds through CLI/MCP/dashboard; stale relevant inputs fail with a recoverable conflict.
exceptions: Unrelated run metadata or displayed stage changes must not invalidate an applicable decision.

rules.principle: Invalidate by dependency rather than by whole-run churn.
rules.appliesWhen: A component, artifact, setting or dependency changes.
rules.action: Recompute applicability only for affected versioned inputs and dependents; retain historical decisions and unaffected accepted versions.
rules.check: Changing an independent component preserves existing applicable approvals; changing a required dependency makes the impact visible.
exceptions: A shared integration/theme dependency can legitimately affect many components when it is actually recorded.

rules.principle: Pin focused revision scope before generation.
rules.appliesWhen: A user requests a localized design change.
rules.action: Persist exact base version/digest, annotation revision, component IDs, instructions, protected areas and acceptance checks; resolve stale bases explicitly.
rules.check: The output has new immutable identity and a checkable change summary; protected areas are compared.
exceptions: Do not guarantee identical surrounding pixels unless the implementation proves it; report unavoidable spillover.

rules.principle: Use artifact coordinates and explicit shape bounds.
rules.appliesWhen: Capturing or persisting annotations.
rules.action: Translate from the actual displayed image to normalized original-image coordinates; use start/latest end for two-point shapes and consistent advertised limits.
rules.check: Check letterboxing, zoom, pan, resize and boundary points; client and server accept the same representation.
exceptions: HTML/PDF annotation uses an immutable image capture with source dependency; never silently reuse an old overlay on a new base.

rules.principle: Decompose into stable components with versioned dependencies.
rules.appliesWhen: A design needs independently reviewable or revisable parts.
rules.action: Assign logical component IDs, exact input versions and an acyclic dependency graph; expose a decomposition preview before dispatch.
rules.check: Independent work can proceed and changed dependencies are detectable without guessing from filenames.
exceptions: Decomposition does not fabricate acceptance of extracted components or require distributed services.

rules.principle: Make batch decisions independently accountable.
rules.appliesWhen: Submitting decisions for several components.
rules.action: Validate each exact component/version and return per-item outcomes plus an idempotent batch receipt; preserve successful independent items.
rules.check: A conflict in one item neither silently accepts it nor discards unrelated successful decisions.
exceptions: A composition still needs integration checks; per-component acceptance does not imply whole-product acceptance.

rules.principle: Separate design autonomy from permissions and money.
rules.appliesWhen: Selecting Guided/YOLO mode or deciding a next action.
rules.action: Persist mode; obtain required guided design decisions or record delegated agent choices; preserve user decisions in either mode and enforce existing scope/cap limits.
rules.check: Every decision identifies its actor; mode changes do not rewrite history or create publication authority.
exceptions: Routine already-authorized work continues without redundant permission requests.

rules.principle: Count design spend in an explicit currency.
rules.appliesWhen: Creating a budget or recording a charge.
rules.action: Separate design from implementation/pack-building costs; record estimates, reservations, settled charges, refunds and unknown exposure with exact arithmetic.
rules.check: The displayed totals reconcile to ledger entries and never treat unknown cost as zero or combine currencies silently.
exceptions: Critique belongs to design spend when configured; conversion requires explicit rate, time and policy.

rules.principle: Reserve bounded cost before controlled dispatch.
rules.appliesWhen: A paid design attempt is about to run.
rules.action: Atomically verify capacity, reserve an admissible bound and persist attempt identity before dispatch through the controlled path.
rules.check: Concurrent admissions cannot claim the same available money; all paid attempts follow the same route.
exceptions: If provider/host charges cannot be bounded or controlled, label enforcement advisory instead of claiming a hard cap.

rules.principle: Reconcile uncertain effects before retrying.
rules.appliesWhen: A billable call times out, crashes or is cancelled.
rules.action: Keep execution identity and unresolved exposure; inspect provider receipts, settle known results and retry only under the explicit duplicate-risk policy.
rules.check: Replaying state or retrying a request does not silently trigger a second paid generation.
exceptions: A cancellation request does not prove stopped billing, failure or refund.

rules.principle: Persist model policy with explicit precedence.
rules.appliesWhen: Starting, resuming or changing run settings.
rules.action: Apply invocation override, persisted run settings, project defaults, personal defaults, then capability/cost-based auto selection; support current-model mode.
rules.check: Resume preserves the run policy and the UI explains inherited versus overridden settings.
exceptions: Applying new defaults to an existing run is an explicit recorded change, not a silent migration.

rules.principle: Report actual model capability and cost uncertainty.
rules.appliesWhen: Assigning a role to a provider/model or choosing a fallback.
rules.action: Validate available modalities/tools, current pricing provenance and permitted fallback; record requested and observed assignments separately.
rules.check: No hardcoded unavailable model or unsupported enforcement claim reaches a worker packet.
exceptions: If the host cannot control selection, state that limitation and use only an allowed compatible fallback.

rules.principle: Bound work and expose the reason for waiting.
rules.appliesWhen: Queuing workers, rendering jobs or provider attempts.
rules.action: Account separately for dependencies, worker slots, rate limits, reservations, cancellation and user holds.
rules.check: Queue depth and wait reason are observable; a saturated subsystem cannot block existing artifact review indefinitely.
exceptions: A queue absorbs bursts but does not create capacity; more workers are not a universal fix.

rules.principle: Use one command policy and stable machine errors.
rules.appliesWhen: Implementing CLI, MCP or HTTP operations.
rules.action: Route adapters through shared validation/handlers; return a stable error identifier, safe details, field location and recovery action.
rules.check: Optional/null/empty fields, bounds and allowed actions have equivalent semantics across interfaces.
exceptions: HTTP Problem Details can be an HTTP mapping; do not impose HTTP status mechanics on every transport.

rules.principle: Commit authoritative state before publishing read views.
rules.appliesWhen: Persisting a workflow transition or refreshing the dashboard.
rules.action: Record state and event/outbox atomically; publish committed facts and rebuild small projections; show the committed result after writes.
rules.check: Crash recovery cannot expose an uncommitted approval; a lagging projection does not undo visible acknowledgement.
exceptions: A full event-sourced architecture or broker is unnecessary to gain transactional records and derived views.

rules.principle: Measure named scenarios before choosing optimizations.
rules.appliesWhen: Setting a performance gate or claiming improvement.
rules.action: Record environment, fixture, cache state, samples and metric; separate computation, transfer, rendering and workflow latency.
rules.check: The comparison uses equivalent conditions and raw observations; synthetic results are not presented as field Web Vitals.
exceptions: Thresholds are profile-specific project targets unless a scoped standard or research result says otherwise.

rules.principle: Avoid rereading unchanged artifact bytes for status.
rules.appliesWhen: Constructing snapshots, history lists or preview metadata.
rules.action: Use bounded projections, pagination and relevant invalidation; keep original blobs out of routine status payloads.
rules.check: The unchanged warm snapshot path performs no original-blob rereads and large history remains bounded.
exceptions: Approval/content-integrity boundaries still verify the relevant actual bytes; preview caches cannot substitute for that evidence.

rules.principle: Match refresh transport to actual update needs.
rules.appliesWhen: Polling or streaming dashboard state.
rules.action: Preserve single-flight cancellation and lifecycle recovery; adapt hidden/idle/error refresh and support revision-based catch-up before adopting streams.
rules.check: There is no overlapping poll or stale overwrite; reconnect restores current state and relevant events.
exceptions: Native EventSource lacks arbitrary Authorization headers; use an appropriate authenticated design and never put capabilities in URLs for convenience.

rules.principle: Cache by sensitivity and immutable identity.
rules.appliesWhen: Setting asset, snapshot or approval cache policy.
rules.action: Distinguish reusable non-sensitive shell assets from private workflow data; invalidate derivatives by source identity.
rules.check: No stale or shared cache can silently substitute a different artifact/decision, and credentials are excluded from cached/exported material.
exceptions: Aggressive asset caching is conditional; do not globally relax private no-store policy because a book recommends caching.

rules.principle: Give mutable state and asynchronous lifetimes explicit owners.
rules.appliesWhen: Refactoring dashboard JavaScript or diagnosing stale work.
rules.action: Separate transport, rendering and draft ownership; copy deliberately, compare identity/revisions and cancel or ignore obsolete callbacks.
rules.check: Repeated open/close and token/run changes leave no unbounded retained work or stale state overwrite.
exceptions: Do not replace understandable code with a class hierarchy, framework or micro-optimization without a concrete benefit.

rules.principle: Make theme lifecycle scoped and reversible.
rules.appliesWhen: Previewing, installing, activating, restoring or removing a theme.
rules.action: Distinguish dashboard, generated-design and OMP-host scope; validate tokens, stage files, preserve originals and record ownership/activation receipts.
rules.check: Restore affects only unchanged receipt-owned additions; conflicts and unavailable host actions are visible.
exceptions: A file copy is not verified host activation; colour preference alone does not authorize replacing host configuration.

rules.principle: Claim only the verification actually performed.
rules.appliesWhen: Reviewing, releasing or reporting completion.
rules.action: Bind each check to exact build/artifacts, method, environment and outcome; distinguish pass/fail/blocked/not-run/deferred and preserve raw evidence.
rules.check: Pack integrity, automated behaviour, host integration and human research are reported separately.
exceptions: Human participant research is deferred by policy; do not fabricate participants or convert missing tooling into a pass.

rules.principle: Preserve recoverable state and ownership across upgrades.
rules.appliesWhen: Migrating, packaging, installing, restoring or collecting retained data.
rules.action: Use copy-first backups, versioned schemas, repeatable migration and complete packaged references; retain versions needed by decisions/revisions/evidence.
rules.check: Old runs remain interpretable, incomplete evidence stays explicit and restore refuses unrelated user changes.
exceptions: Do not manufacture legacy approvals/budgets; SQLite WAL stays on a supported local same-host filesystem.
